title: Basic English — Course 2, Semester 2 — Pilot Variant 5

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. Where will the information meeting take place?
tasks.audioText: The town council is asking residents to comment on a proposed cycle route between the railway station and the college area. An information meeting will take place at the civic centre next Monday at six in the evening. Maps will be available at the entrance. Residents can also submit comments online until the end of the following week.

tasks.prompt: Listening 2. How long will online comments be accepted?
tasks.audioText: The town council is asking residents to comment on a proposed cycle route between the railway station and the college area. An information meeting will take place at the civic centre next Monday at six in the evening. Maps will be available at the entrance. Residents can also submit comments online until the end of the following week.
options: Until the end of the following week

tasks.prompt: A town transport survey found that many college students travelled by car because the bus service did not match lesson times. The council is considering a cycle route and a revised bus timetable. Some residents support the cycle route because it could reduce traffic near the college, while others are concerned about road crossings. The council says that safety assessments will be completed before a final decision is made. Reading 1. Why did some students travel by car?
options: Parking near the college was expensive
The bus timetable did not match lesson times
The college car park was closed during the survey
Students were required to carry large equipment

tasks.prompt: What must happen before the council makes a final decision?
options: A public vote must be held first
The cycle route must be built immediately
The cycle route had already been approved

tasks.prompt: The proposed route ___ before construction begins.
Choose TWO points that should be considered when planning a cycle route.
options: The colour of nearby shop signs

tasks.prompt: A planned system for moving people around a town is a transport ___.
You want to comment on the proposal politely. Which sentence is best?
options: This plan is stupid and nobody should discuss it.
I would like to support the proposal, provided that the crossings are made safe.
I have no evidence, but the council is wrong.
Build it exactly where I say.

tasks.prompt: Put the stages of community transport in a logical order.
options: Collect information about current travel patterns
Review feedback before making a decision
correctOrder: Collect information about current travel patterns
Review feedback before making a decision

tasks.prompt: Write 80–100 words giving your opinion on a proposed improvement to local transport. Include one benefit, one concern and a possible solution.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total: a proposed transport improvement is identified and one benefit is explained (0–2); one realistic concern and a possible solution are included (0–2); the opinion is balanced and logically linked with understandable grammar (0–2); transport/community-planning vocabulary, spelling and punctuation are appropriate (0–2).
